scenes.say: Joins are everywhere in SQL. Which join fits your query—and what’s the classic mistake engineers make?

scenes.label: INNER
scenes.sub: Only rows with matching keys in both tables
scenes.say: Inner join returns only rows with matching keys in both tables.
Left join keeps all rows from the left table, filling in NULLs where there’s no match on the right. Right join is the opposite.

scenes.title: Forgot Join Condition
scenes.say: If you forget the join condition, SQL creates a Cartesian product—every possible combination. That’s a disaster in interviews.

scenes.question: What does NULL mean in LEFT JOIN?
scenes.wrong: It's a missing row in both tables.
scenes.right: It means no matching row on the right table.
scenes.say: In a left join, NULL means the left table row has no match on the right. Don’t mix this up.
